query:
Find applicable evidence-backed ways to reduce execution time in this GitHub Actions workflow. Consider its jobs, dependencies, commands, triggers, and repository manifests.
name: Mark stale issues and pull requests

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "30 2 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  stale:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Mark stale items
        uses: actions/stale@v11
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          stale-issue-message: "This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity occurs."
          stale-pr-message: "This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity occurs."
          close-issue-message: "This issue was closed because it has been stale for 14 days with no activity."
          close-pr-message: "This pull request was closed because it has been stale for 14 days with no activity."
          days-before-issue-stale: 30
          days-before-pr-stale: 30
          days-before-issue-close: 14
          days-before-pr-close: 14
          stale-issue-label: stale
          stale-pr-label: stale
          exempt-issue-labels: pinned,security,no-stale-check
          exempt-pr-labels: pinned,security,no-stale-check
          remove-stale-when-updated: true
          operations-per-run: 200

results.content:
Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows

Pattern: P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE (failing_schedule_suppression)

When is pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows applicable?

Assess pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: A monitored pause/resume policy is approved

Contraindications: Continuous monitoring or periodic checks are mandatory

Method: Notify the owner when pausing; Define an explicit recovery and reactivation path

Reported finding: Failure-streak suppression offers estimated savings.

Reported metrics: {"consecutive_failure_threshold": 3, "paid_total_vm_time_reduction_percent": 3.2}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.3.1; Tables 5-6; PDF pp. 8, 9: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

Literature example before:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
keep running a repeatedly failing scheduled workflow


Literature example after:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
pause after an approved failure streak and notify the owner


Literature example diff:

--- knowledge/examples/P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE/before.txt
+++ knowledge/examples/P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE/after.txt
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 # ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
-keep running a repeatedly failing scheduled workflow
+pause after an approved failure streak and notify the owner
contraindications: Continuous monitoring or periodic checks are mandatory
preconditions: A monitored pause/resume policy is approved

results.content:
Suppress schedules during repository inactivity

Pattern: P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE (scheduled_run_reduction)

When is suppress schedules during repository inactivity applicable?

Assess suppress schedules during repository inactivity for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Periodic results depend only on repository changes

Contraindications: External dependencies, security or time-based requirements need fresh checks

Method: Identify meaningful activity rather than generated self-updates; Resume when relevant inputs change

Reported finding: Inactivity suppression saves some scheduled work.

Reported metrics: {"paid_scheduled_vm_time_reduction_percent": 1.1}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.3.2; Table 5; PDF pp. 8, 9: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

Literature example before:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
run on every schedule tick


Literature example after:

# ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
run on a tick only if relevant activity occurred


Literature example diff:

--- knowledge/examples/P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE/before.txt
+++ knowledge/examples/P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE/after.txt
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 # ANALYST ILLUSTRATION; NOT PAPER CODE; NOT EXECUTED
-run on every schedule tick
+run on a tick only if relevant activity occurred
contraindications: External dependencies, security or time-based requirements need fresh checks
preconditions: Periodic results depend only on repository changes
